jp: 家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}{かえったら|tara-conditional}、すぐ手[て]{を|o-object}洗[あら]ってください。
en: When you get home, please wash your hands right away.
why: A request in the main clause rules out と; たら marks the step that must be finished first.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{が|ga-sub-clause}{おわったら/おわれば|tara-conditional}、おやつ{を|o-object}食[た]べましょう。
en: When the homework is finished, let's have a snack.
why: A suggestion (let's) after a finished step needs たら; と cannot lead into an invitation.

jp: 箱[はこ]{を|o-object}{あけたら/あけると|tara-conditional}、中[なか]{に|ni-location}手紙[てがみ]{が|ga-subject}入[はい]っていました。
en: When I opened the box, there was a letter inside.
why: A past discovery after an action takes たら (or と); ば cannot describe what actually turned up.

jp: 目[め]{が|ga-sub-clause}{さめたら/さめると|tara-conditional}、もう九時[くじ]でした。
en: When I woke up, it was already nine o'clock.
why: Finding something unexpected after waking is a past discovery, which takes たら (or と).

jp: 駅[えき]{に/へ|ni-destination}{ついたら|tara-conditional}、電話[でんわ]{を|o-object}してください。
en: When you arrive at the station, please call me.
why: The request follows the arrival, so たら is needed; と and なら do not fit a request after arriving.

jp: 子[こ]どもたち{が|ga-sub-clause}{ねたら|tara-conditional}、洗濯[せんたく]{を|o-object}します。
en: When the children have gone to sleep, I'll do the laundry.
why: My own planned action after a finished event takes たら; と cannot be followed by a will or plan.

jp: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]{が|ga-sub-clause}{かわいたら/かわけば|tara-conditional}、すぐたたみます。
en: Once the laundry is dry, I'll fold it right away.
why: My intended action once something is complete takes たら; と cannot lead into a plan.

jp: 大人[おとな]{に|ni-change}{なったら|tara-conditional}、何[なに]{に|ni-change}なりたいです{か|ka-question}。
en: What do you want to be when you grow up?
why: A wish or question about the future after a state is reached takes たら, not と.

jp: 明日[あした]雨[あめ]{が|ga-sub-clause}{ふったら/ふれば|tara-conditional}、家[いえ]{で|de-place}映画[えいが]{を|o-object}見[み]ましょう。
en: If it rains tomorrow, let's watch a movie at home.
why: A one-off hypothetical followed by 'let's' takes たら; と cannot be followed by an invitation.

jp: 台所[だいどころ]{に/へ|ni-destination}{いったら/いくと|tara-conditional}、父[ちち]{が|ga-subject}料理[りょうり]{を|o-object}していました。
en: When I went to the kitchen, my father was cooking.
why: A past discovery after going somewhere takes たら (or と); ば and なら do not report what was found.

jp: お風呂[ふろ]{に|ni-destination}{はいったら|tara-conditional}、早[はや]く寝[ね]なさい。
en: Go to bed early after you have had your bath.
why: The command comes after the bath is finished, so たら; なら would put the bath first and と cannot take a command.

jp: 熱[ねつ]{が|ga-sub-clause}{さがったら/さがれば|tara-conditional}、学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]ってもいいです{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: Once your fever has gone down, you can go to school.
why: Permission that depends on something happening first takes たら; と cannot be followed by permission.

jp: 夕[ゆう]ご飯[はん]{が|ga-sub-clause}{できたら|tara-conditional}、呼[よ]びます{よ/ね|yo-assertion}。
en: I'll call you when dinner is ready.
why: A promise of what I will do once something is complete takes たら; と cannot be followed by a will.

jp: 時間[じかん]{が|ga-existence}{あれば/あったら|ba-conditional}、買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きましょう。
en: If we have time, let's go shopping.
why: A condition followed by an invitation needs ば (or たら); と cannot lead into 'let's'.

jp: {やすければ/やすかったら|ba-conditional}、このソファー{を|o-object}買[か]います。
en: If it's cheap, I'll buy this sofa.
why: An adjective condition followed by my decision takes ければ; と cannot be followed by a will.

jp: 明日[あした]{はれれば/はれたら|ba-conditional}、洗濯物[せんたくもの]{を|o-object}外[そと]{に/で|ni-location}干[ほ]します。
en: If it's fine tomorrow, I'll hang the laundry outside.
why: A weather condition followed by a plan takes ば or たら; と cannot lead into a plan.

jp: もっと早[はや]く{ねれば/ねたら|ba-conditional}よかったです。
en: I should have gone to bed earlier.
why: Regret is expressed with ばよかった (or たらよかった); と cannot express 'should have'.

jp: もっと勉強[べんきょう]{すれば/したら|ba-conditional}よかった{と|to-quote}思[おも]います。
en: I think I should have studied more.
why: ばよかった expresses regret about what was not done; と and なら cannot do that.

jp: 傘[かさ]{を|o-object}持[も]って{いけば/いったら|ba-conditional}よかったです。
en: I should have taken an umbrella.
why: The regret pattern is ばよかった; と and なら cannot mean 'should have'.

jp: もう少[すこ]し早[はや]く家[いえ]{を|o-departure}{でれば/でたら|ba-conditional}、間[ま]に合[あ]った{のに|noni-although}。
en: If I had left home a little earlier, I would have made it.
why: A contrary-to-fact condition with a past result takes ば or たら; と cannot report what did not happen.

jp: 料理[りょうり]{は|wa-topic}{つくれば|ba-conditional}作[つく]る{ほど|ba-hodo}上手[じょうず]{に|ni-change}なります。
en: The more you cook, the better you get at it.
why: The pattern 〜ば〜ほど (the more…, the more…) uses the ば form of the verb.

jp: この歌[うた]{は|wa-topic}{きけば|ba-conditional}聞[き]く{ほど|ba-hodo}好[す]き{に|ni-change}なります。
en: The more I listen to this song, the more I like it.
why: 〜ば〜ほど needs the ば form before the repeated verb.

jp: 部屋[へや]{は|wa-topic}{かたづければ|ba-conditional}片付[かたづ]ける{ほど|ba-hodo}広[ひろ]く感[かん]じます。
en: The more you tidy the room, the more spacious it feels.
why: The proportional pattern 〜ば〜ほど requires the ば form.

jp: 天気[てんき]{が|ga-sub-clause}{よければ/よかったら|ba-conditional}、庭[にわ]{で|de-place}ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}食[た]べましょう。
en: If the weather is nice, let's eat in the garden.
why: An adjective condition followed by an invitation takes ければ or たら; と cannot lead into 'let's'.

jp: ゆっくり{やすめば/やすむと/やすんだら|ba-conditional}、すぐ元気[げんき]{に|ni-change}なります{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: If you rest properly, you'll be better soon.
why: A general cause and result takes ば; なら would mean 'if you are going to rest', which is not the point.

jp: 洗濯機[せんたくき]{は|wa-topic}どのボタン{を|o-object}{おせば/おしたら|ba-conditional}いいですか。
en: Which button on the washing machine should I press?
why: Asking what to do uses ばいい (or たらいい); なら cannot form 'what should I do'.

jp: 窓[まど]{を|o-object}{あけると/あけたら|to-conditional}、冷[つめ]たい風[かぜ]{が|ga-subject}入[はい]ってきました。
en: When I opened the window, a cold wind blew in.
why: An action followed at once by an unplanned result takes と; ば cannot report a past event.

jp: この道[みち]{を|o-path}まっすぐ{いくと/いけば/いったら|to-conditional}、右[みぎ]{に|ni-location}郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: If you go straight along this road, there's a post office on the right.
why: Directions (do A and you will find B) take と; なら would mean 'if you are planning to go', which does not fit.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]{おきると/おきたら|to-conditional}、まず水[みず]{を|o-object}一杯[いっぱい]飲[の]みます。
en: Every morning, when I get up, I first drink a glass of water.
why: A habitual sequence (whenever A, then B) takes と; ば and なら do not describe a routine.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}眠[ねむ]く{なると/なったら|to-conditional}、すぐ機嫌[きげん]{が|ga-subject}悪[わる]くなります。
en: My little brother gets grumpy as soon as he gets sleepy.
why: A reliable pattern (whenever A, B happens) takes と; なら would mean 'if you are going to be sleepy'.

jp: 春[はる]{に|ni-change}{なると/なれば/なったら|to-conditional}、庭[にわ]{の|no-possessive}花[はな]{が|ga-subject}いっせいに咲[さ]きます。
en: When spring comes, the flowers in the garden all bloom at once.
why: A natural, automatic result takes と; なら does not fit a natural process.

jp: このボタン{を|o-object}{おすと/おせば/おしたら|to-conditional}、お湯[ゆ]{が|ga-subject}出[で]ます。
en: If you press this button, hot water comes out.
why: A mechanism with an automatic result takes と; なら would mean 'if you plan to press it'.

jp: ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}{たべすぎると/たべすぎれば/たべすぎたら|to-conditional}、眠[ねむ]くなります。
en: If you eat too much, you get sleepy.
why: A general cause and effect takes と; なら would mean 'if you are going to overeat', which is not intended.

jp: 冬[ふゆ]{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]{に|ni-change}{なると/なったら|to-conditional}、すぐ寒[さむ]くなります。
en: In winter, it gets cold quickly once night comes.
why: A recurring natural change takes と; なら does not suit a natural process.

jp: 家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}{かえると/かえったら|to-conditional}、玄関[げんかん]{に|ni-location}荷物[にもつ]{が|ga-subject}届[とど]いていました。
en: When I got home, a parcel had been delivered to the entrance.
why: Coming home and finding something is a past discovery, which takes と; ば and なら do not fit.

jp: 部屋[へや]{の|no-possessive}電気[でんき]{を|o-object}{つけると/つけたら|to-conditional}、虫[むし]{が|ga-subject}たくさん飛[と]んでいました。
en: When I turned on the light in the room, lots of insects were flying around.
why: An action followed by an unexpected sight takes と; ば and なら do not fit a past discovery.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}お酒[さけ]{を|o-object}{のむと/のんだら/のめば|to-conditional}、すぐ顔[かお]{が|ga-subject}赤[あか]くなります。
en: When my father drinks alcohol, his face turns red right away.
why: A habitual or natural reaction takes と; なら would mean 'if he is going to drink', which does not fit.

jp: 窓[まど]{を|o-object}{しめると/しめれば/しめたら|to-conditional}、外[そと]{の|no-possessive}音[おと]{が|ga-sense}聞[き]こえなくなります。
en: If you close the window, you can no longer hear the noise outside.
why: A direct cause and effect takes と; なら would mean 'if you are going to close it'.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]{が|ga-sub-clause}{ふると/ふれば/ふったら|to-conditional}、家[いえ]{で|de-place}ゆっくり過[す]ごします。
en: On Sundays, if it rains, I relax at home.
why: A habitual pattern (whenever A, B) takes と; なら would mean 'if you say it will rain'.

jp: 留学[りゅうがく]{するなら|nara-conditional}、先[さき]に英語[えいご]{を|o-object}勉強[べんきょう]した方[ほう]がいいです{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: If you're going to study abroad, you should study English first.
why: A plan stated by the listener, with advice about what to do before it, takes なら.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]{に|ni-purpose}{いくなら|nara-conditional}、前[まえ]{の|no-possessive}日[ひ]{に|ni-time}荷物[にもつ]{を|o-object}用意[ようい]しておきなさい。
en: If you're going on a trip, get your luggage ready the day before.
why: The preparation comes before the trip, so a plan with なら is needed; たら and と would put the trip first.

jp: 外[そと]{で|de-place}{たべるなら|nara-conditional}、予約[よやく]{を|o-object}した方[ほう]がいいです{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: If you're going to eat out, it's better to make a reservation.
why: The booking must come before eating, so なら (if you are going to) is right.

jp: 家[いえ]{を|o-object}{かうなら|nara-conditional}、お金[かね]{を|o-object}貯[た]めておかなければなりません。
en: If you're going to buy a house, you have to save money beforehand.
why: Saving comes before buying, so なら sets the plan; たら would put the purchase first.

jp: 母[はは]{が|ga-sub-clause}{でかけるなら|nara-conditional}、夕[ゆう]ご飯[はん]{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{が|ga-subject}作[つく]ります。
en: If Mother is going out, I'll make dinner.
why: A statement of someone's plan answered with my own decision takes なら; と cannot lead into a will.

jp: あなた{が|ga-sub-clause}{いくなら|nara-conditional}、私[わたし]{も|mo-also}行[い]きます。
en: If you're going, I'll go too.
why: Reacting to the listener's stated plan takes なら; と cannot be followed by a decision.

jp: 犬[いぬ]{を|o-object}{かうなら|nara-conditional}、先[さき]に家族[かぞく]{と|to-with}よく話[はな]し合[あ]ってください。
en: If you're going to get a dog, please talk it over with your family first.
why: The talk comes before getting the dog, so なら is needed; たら would mean after getting it.

jp: 車[くるま]{を|o-object}運転[うんてん]{するなら|nara-conditional}、お酒[さけ]{は|wa-contrast}飲[の]まないでください。
en: If you're going to drive, please don't drink alcohol.
why: Not drinking applies before driving, so the plan is set up with なら.

jp: 髪[かみ]{を|o-object}{きるなら|nara-conditional}、この美容院[びよういん]{が|ga-subject}いいです{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: If you're getting a haircut, this salon is good.
why: Recommending something for the listener's plan takes なら; たら would mean after the haircut.

jp: 買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}{いくなら|nara-conditional}、帰[かえ]り{に|ni-time}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{を|o-object}買[か]ってきてください。
en: If you're going shopping, please buy milk on the way back.
why: A request tied to the listener's stated plan takes なら; と cannot be followed by a request.

jp: ケーキ{を|o-object}{つくるなら|nara-conditional}、先[さき]に材料[ざいりょう]{を|o-object}そろえておきましょう。
en: If you're going to make a cake, let's get the ingredients ready first.
why: Gathering ingredients comes before making the cake, so なら is right.

jp: お風呂[ふろ]{に|ni-destination}{はいるなら|nara-conditional}、先[さき]にタオル{を|o-object}出[だ]しておいてください。
en: If you're going to take a bath, please put out a towel first.
why: The towel comes before the bath, so なら; たら would put the bath first.

jp: ごみ{を|o-object}{だすなら|nara-conditional}、朝[あさ]八時[はちじ]{までに|madeni-deadline}持[も]って行[い]ってください。
en: If you're putting out the rubbish, please take it out by eight in the morning.
why: A request about the listener's plan to put out rubbish takes なら; と cannot be followed by a request.
